title: Rigveda 10.151: Hymn to faith (Shraddha)
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.151: Hymn to faith (Shraddha): Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.151 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to faith. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 135r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
This manuscript inserts khila verses (supplementary hymns outside Aufrecht's text) at some hymn ends; they are noted in the section notes and not reproduced.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.151.1-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 9); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 135r
translation.original_text:
1śra̱ddhayā̱gniḥ sam i̍dhyate śra̱ddhayā̍ hūyate ha̱viḥ | śra̱ddhām bhaga̍sya mū̱rdhani̱ vaca̱sā ve̍dayāmasi ||
2pri̱yaṁ śra̍ddhe̱ dada̍taḥ pri̱yaṁ śra̍ddhe̱ didā̍sataḥ | pri̱yam bho̱jeṣu̱ yajva̍sv i̱dam ma̍ udi̱taṁ kṛ̍dhi ||
3yathā̍ de̱vā asu̍reṣu śra̱ddhām u̱greṣu̍ cakri̱re | e̱vam bho̱jeṣu̱ yajva̍sv a̱smāka̍m udi̱taṁ kṛ̍dhi ||
4śra̱ddhāṁ de̱vā yaja̍mānā vā̱yugo̍pā̱ upā̍sate | śra̱ddhāṁ hṛ̍da̱yya1̱̍yākū̍tyā śra̱ddhayā̍ vindate̱ vasu̍ ||
5śra̱ddhām prā̱tar ha̍vāmahe śra̱ddhām ma̱dhyaṁdi̍na̱m pari̍ | śra̱ddhāṁ sūrya̍sya ni̱mruci̱ śraddhe̱ śrad dhā̍paye̱ha na̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1By Faith is Agni kindled, through Faith is oblation offered up. We celebrate with praises Faith upon the height of happiness.
2Bless thou the man who gives, O Faith; Faith, bless the man who fain would give. Bless thou the liberal worshippers: bless thou the word that I have said.
3Even as the Deities maintained Faith in the mighty Asuras, So make this uttered wish of mine true for the liberal worshippers.
4Guarded by Vâyu, Gods and men who sacrifice draw near to Faith. Man winneth Faith by yearnings of the heart, and opulence by Faith.
5Faith in the early morning, Faith at noonday will we invocate, Faith at the setting of the Sun. O Faith, endow us with belief.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 135r (OPenn image 134, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.151.1 ‹śraddhayāgniḥ sam idhyate śraddhayā›. 10.151.5 ends in line 6 with a varga number, followed by the heading khilaṃ and the Medha khila (medhāṃ mahyam aṅgiraso), which runs to 136r line 5. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 136r, begins in RV 10.152.1 ‹śāsa itthā mahām̐ asy›. Verses 10.151.1-5 end on this page.
